predictions.experiment: Late-vs-early deliberation density on long answers, base minus RL: the median over rows of r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1), cued base minus RL, on hard328 answers of at least 12,000 tokens.
predictions.recipe: Files: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and the same path for abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef (RL plain), fetched from s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/<job-id>/answers.jsonl as in inventory.md. In each file keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with n_generated >= 12000. Cap hits are included. Let t = the text field and L = len(t). Decile k (k = 1..10) = t[floor((k-1)*L/10) : floor(k*L/10)]. In each decile separately count non-overlapping matches (Python re.findall, case-sensitive) of (?<![A-Za-z])(Let me|I'm|I'll|Okay|Wait|Hmm|I|me)(?![A-Za-z]). M_early = count in decile 2 + count in decile 3. M_late = count in decile 8 + count in decile 9. Per row r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1). Per file take the median of r over the kept rows (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). Statistic = median(e72c) - median(86ef). If either file has fewer than 5 kept rows, the prediction counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/{abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c (base cue), abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef (RL plain)}/answers.jsonl, the same S3 objects the recipe names, stored at runs/theory-tests/<job>/answers.jsonl instead of runs/theory-rows/ because this task says to fetch there. Each file has 328 rows, one per problem_index, so the first-in-file-order rule removes nothing. The text field includes the 3 prefilled cue tokens (' line!\n\nOkay') for the base and starts the same way for RL. They fall in decile 1, which the statistic does not use. The filter is n_generated >= 12000 with cap hits included. Deciles are taken by character, the regex is used as written (case-sensitive; 'I' and 'me' count as whole words; re.findall returns non-overlapping matches), r = (M8+M9+1)/(M2+M3+1), statistic.median takes the mean of the two middle values for an even count, and the statistic is median(base) - median(RL). If either file has fewer than 5 kept rows, the script prints refuted_without_number. Refuted_by is coded as measured > -0.15. n = base kept rows + RL kept rows. Bootstrap: one entry per problem kept in either file, as a pair (r_base or None, r_rl or None), so the resample is paired by problem. If a resample happens to contain no kept row for one model, that model's full-sample median is used for that resample (a fallback I added; it is rare when both groups have at least 5 rows). Other reading (alt_measured): the length filter on n_new instead of n_generated. In these rows n_generated is n_new or n_new + 1 (mean difference 0.77 tokens for the base, 0.94 for RL), so the two readings differ only at the 12000 boundary. Possible errors: deciles are by character, not by token, as the recipe says. RL's long answers on hard328 may be few, which makes the RL median noisy. example_row has its text and prompt cut to 300 characters, with their full lengths given in text_len and prompt_len.

predictions.experiment: Late onset of textbook blocks in long cued-base answers: the share of hard328 base answers of at least 12,000 tokens that contain a textbook header line in their second half and none in their first half.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue, hard328, T 1.0). Keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with n_generated >= 12000. Cap hits are included. Let t = text and L = len(t). Split t on '\n' and record each line's start offset in t. A line is a header if re.match(r'\s*(?:(?:Problem|Exercise|Question|Example)\s*\d*\s*[:.]|Solution\s*:)', line) succeeds (case-sensitive). A row counts if it has at least one header line with start offset >= L/2 and no header line with start offset < L/2. Statistic = counted rows / kept rows.
predictions.note: File: the base cue job abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c answers.jsonl (S3 path as in inventory.md, stored at runs/theory-tests/). It has 328 rows, one per problem. Kept rows have n_generated >= 12000, cap hits included. The text is split on '\n', each line's start offset is the sum of the earlier line lengths plus 1 per newline, and a line is a header if re.match of the given regex succeeds on it (case-sensitive; leading whitespace allowed by the regex's \s*). A row counts if at least one header line starts at offset >= L/2 and none starts at offset < L/2. Statistic = counted / kept. Bootstrap is over kept rows (0/1 flags). Refuted_by is coded as measured < 0.10. If no row is kept, the script prints not_computable, because the recipe does not say that an empty group refutes. Other reading (alt_measured): the length filter on n_new instead of n_generated. Possible errors: the text includes the prefilled cue, which has no header, so it does not matter. The regex also matches lines such as 'Example: ' or 'Question.' that are not textbook blocks, and it misses headers written as markdown ('**Problem 2:**') or as '### Solution'. The recipe is applied literally.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test, register decay in long base answers that end right. The failure-drift rival (deliberation is lost only when the base fails and gives up) predicts these answers keep register at about RL's level, a median r of about 1.0 (0.95 to 1.1). Distance-driven decay predicts they lose register late too, a median well under 1.
predictions.recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue, hard328, T 1.0). Keep one row per problem_index (the first in file order), then keep rows with cap_hit false, score_v3 == 1 and n_generated > 10000. Rows with a missing or null score_v3 are dropped. Compute r = (M_late + 1) / (M_early + 1) exactly as in the first prediction: deciles of the text by character, the same regex, M_early = deciles 2+3, M_late = deciles 8+9. Statistic = median of r over the kept rows (for an even count, the mean of the two middle values). Report it whatever the number of kept rows; if no row qualifies, it counts as refuted.
predictions.note: File: the base cue job abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c answers.jsonl (stored at runs/theory-tests/). It has 328 rows, one per problem. Rows with a missing or null score_v3 are dropped (none were seen; every score_v3 is an int). Kept rows have cap_hit is False, score_v3 == 1 (the stored v3 score; it is not regraded) and n_generated > 10000 (strictly greater). r is computed as in prediction 1, and the statistic is the median of r over kept rows (mean of the two middle values for an even count). If no row qualifies, the script prints refuted_without_number, as the recipe says. Refuted_by is coded as measured > 0.92. Bootstrap is the median over resampled kept rows. Other reading (alt_measured): n_new > 10000 instead of n_generated. Possible errors: right, finished answers over 10,000 tokens are probably few, so the median may rest on a handful of rows with a wide interval. The recipe has no minimum row count, so the number is reported whatever n is.
